title: Yosi bar Menashya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In the Jerusalem Talmud, Sukkah chapter 3, at the end of halakhah 2, the names are given as “R' Hinena, R' Pinekh, Rav Matna, Yosi bar Menashya, in the name of Rav.”[^1] In Megillah chapter 2, halakhah 4, the wording is “R' Helbo, Rav Yosi bar Minisha, in the name of Rav.” It is possible that he is the one called in the Babylonian Talmud Rav Yosi son of Rav Menashya of Dewil, who was a student of Rav, as in Kiddushin 79b and Niddah 26b.[^2]

notes.text: Hyman cites the end of Sukkah 3:2. Guggenheimer’s text there concerns the myrtle and does not contain this chain. Hinena and Pinekh render his חיננא and פינך.
Menashya and Minisha reproduce מנשיא and מינישא. ‘Of Dewil’ follows מדויל; the place designation is uncertain.
